provenance.mode: MODE-OFF (no --sync; active_snapshot absent per schema.json 3-state rule). Target has no VCS, so SNAPSHOT_ID would be content-addressed; pinning was not requested.
provenance.execution: Stages run inline/sequentially by the orchestrator, per mantis-researcher Step 2's documented fallback ('If sub-agents or concurrency are not supported by the current environment, fall back to performing the sweeps and deep-dives sequentially'), because the harness caps concurrency.
provenance.triage_rule_mapping: FP-01..FP-13 map one-to-one and in order onto mantis-review Step 3's 13 negative constraints (FP-01 ignore_hypothetical_misuse ... FP-13 verify_attacker_control_of_source). 'answer' states whether that rule's own stated condition holds for the finding: for the twelve dismissal rules, DOES_NOT_HOLD means the rule does not knock the finding out; for FP-08 (intrinsic_security_flaws, the one save rule) HOLDS means its keep-it-anyway condition applies.
stages_run: mantis-meta-agent (supervisor; pass 1, MODE-OFF, state written to workspace/.mantis_state.json)
mantis-summarize (per-directory security map; written under workspace/, NOT into the target)
mantis-threat-model (workspace/kb/THREAT_MODEL.md; Intent: PRODUCTION via the 5-check production-signal checklist)
mantis-researcher (sequential Wave-1 triage + Wave-2 deep audit over all 55 files; grep fallback for the structural index)
mantis-dedupe (signature = sha256(normalized_title|cwe|primary_target); no cross-pass archive to fold against on pass 1)
mantis-review (13 negative constraints applied adversarially; 17 candidates killed, see ruled_out)
mantis-critic (production viability; Intent: PRODUCTION so no SAMPLE_OR_TEST dismissal)
mantis-chain (one super-finding: ledger-flow unauthenticated import to unauthenticated stored XSS)
mantis-calibrate (Mantis Risk Score per finding, recorded in the workspace finding JSONs)
mantis-reflect (no per-subagent transcript logs exposed by this harness; recorded as a missing-transcript insight per the skill's explicit instruction)
stages_skipped: mantis-history: the target is a plain directory with no VCS metadata (git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree fails), so vcs_type = none and there is no history to mine for past vulnerability patterns.

mantis-structural-index: no SCIP/Kythe/compiler/ctags backend is available offline. The skill declares the index HINT-only and degrades to grep, so the researcher's mandatory repo-wide grep floor was used for every call-site sweep instead.

mantis-reproduce: cannot run offline. No Go toolchain, Python venv, Node modules, Postgres/Redis, container runtime or network is available, and the operator forbade writing under the target tree, so no PoC could be executed. Every finding therefore carries repro_status not_attempted, never failed_to_reproduce (the skill's absent-evidence rule routes to not_attempted, never to a negative verdict).
mantis-patch: skipped by operator instruction (TARGET is read-only). No fix was generated or applied, so the re-attack bypass loop was not entered either.
mantis-advise / mantis-pipeline-adapter: not pipeline stages (guidance documents for building custom harnesses).

ruled_out.assertion: SQL injection in the account-balance query via the f-string interpolation of account_id
ruled_out.killed_by: The route is declared `@api_bp.get("/accounts/<int:account_id>/balance")`; Flask's `int` converter only matches digits and hands the view a Python int, so nothing non-numeric can reach the f-string. The mitigation works, so rule 09 dismisses it.

ruled_out.assertion: Path traversal in the importer's staged-file resolution
ruled_out.killed_by: `_staged_path` calls `os.path.realpath` on the join and requires the result to start with `realpath(root) + os.sep`, which defeats both `..` segments and an absolute `name` (join returns the absolute path, whose realpath fails the prefix test). Rule 09 credits the working mitigation.

The function's own docstring says the migration removed the last caller, and a repo-wide grep confirms zero call sites. Nothing reaches it, and it is not an injection/secret/broken-algorithm case, so rule 08 does not rescue it and rule 01 applies.

ruled_out.assertion: SQL injection through the LIMIT clause of ListDevices
ruled_out.killed_by: The only caller (`handlers/device.go:38-45`) parses the value with `strconv.Atoi`, requires `n > 0 && n <= 500`, and re-serialises with `strconv.Itoa`, so the interpolated string is always decimal digits. The round trip is an effective mitigation.

ruled_out.assertion: Billing webhook compares the signature against a stale digest (hmac.Equal(got, mac.Sum(nil)) after want was computed)
ruled_out.killed_by: `hash.Hash.Sum` appends the current digest to its argument without mutating the underlying state, so the second `mac.Sum(nil)` returns the same bytes as `want`. The comparison is correct, is constant-time via `hmac.Equal`, and is preceded by a 300-second timestamp check.

ruled_out.assertion: TLS verification disabled in the billing HTTP client
ruled_out.killed_by: `Env` is declared `const Env = "production"` at main.go:24, so `Env == "sandbox"` is a compile-time-false branch that never executes in this build. There is no reachable path to the InsecureSkipVerify transport.

ruled_out.assertion: Path traversal in the landing-page slug handler
ruled_out.killed_by: `safe_slug` enforces `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$` before the join (deps.py:7, 72-75), which admits no dot, slash or backslash. The mitigation blocks the traversal class outright.

ruled_out.assertion: Reflected XSS in the unsubscribe landing page
ruled_out.killed_by: The token is inserted into element text with `<` and `>` replaced by entities. Without an angle bracket no tag or attribute context can be opened, and there is no attribute or script context at the sink.

ruled_out.assertion: SQL injection through the LIMIT clause of listNotifications
ruled_out.killed_by: The route declares a Fastify JSON schema with `limit: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1, maximum: 200, default: 50 }` and `additionalProperties: false` (routes/notifications.js:6-15); Fastify coerces and validates before the handler runs, so only a bounded integer reaches the template literal.

ruled_out.assertion: Hardcoded API token in the service configuration (defaults.demoToken)
ruled_out.killed_by: The value is `pulse-sample-token-for-docs` under a `defaults` block and is never read by any authentication path — `plugins/auth.js` resolves sessions only through `store.findSessionByHash`. Rule 02's hardcoded-mock exemption applies; its exposure through the unauthenticated /admin/config route is already covered by the admin-scope finding.

The helper takes a complete SQL string by contract and its comment says it is used by one-off migration scripts under ops/. A repo-wide grep finds no HTTP-layer caller, so reaching it requires a hypothetical future caller passing untrusted SQL.

ruled_out.assertion: Asset-host allowlist bypass via URL userinfo (https://assets.orchard.example@evil.example/)
ruled_out.killed_by: `new URL(...).hostname` returns the authority host, which is `evil.example` in that construction, so the `ASSET_HOSTS` set check rejects it. The allowlist works on the submission path; the real defect is the retry path that never calls this validator, reported separately.

ruled_out.assertion: SQS queue policy grants sqs:SendMessage to AnyPrincipal
ruled_out.killed_by: The statement is guarded by `conditions: { ArnEquals: { 'aws:SourceArn': props.eventBusArn } }`, the documented cross-account EventBridge pattern, and `data-stack.ts:34-36` never passes `eventBusArn`, so the branch does not execute in any synthesised stack.

ruled_out.assertion: Hardcoded API key in the environment configuration (docs.exampleApiKey)
ruled_out.killed_by: The constant sits in an object whose JSDoc reads 'Values shown in the onboarding guide; not read by any stack', and a repo-wide grep confirms `docs` has no consumer. Rule 02's documentation/mock exemption applies.

ruled_out.assertion: Unbounded in-memory rate-limiter maps allow memory exhaustion
ruled_out.killed_by: Neither module's stated purpose is DoS defence and the finding is a missing size bound on a cache, which rule 07 excludes. The same reasoning covers pulse-notify/plugins/ratelimit.js:29.

ruled_out.assertion: Missing security headers and verbose error messages across the services
ruled_out.killed_by: Reflecting `err.message` and omitting CSP/HSTS are the defence-in-depth and hygiene items rule 02 excludes; no specific secret was shown to flow into an error path.

ruled_out.assertion: Unhandled ValueError on the postings limit parameter
ruled_out.killed_by: `int(request.args.get("limit", 100))` raises on non-numeric input and yields a 500. That is an input-robustness/availability nit with no data-integrity or confidentiality consequence, which rules 07 and 02 exclude.

findings.title: Maintenance API is unauthenticated: the internal-token guard matches a prefix the blueprint is not mounted under
findings.evidence: `INTERNAL_PREFIX = "/internal"` (auth.py:13) and the guard returns early unless `request.path.startswith(INTERNAL_PREFIX)` (auth.py:55). `app.py:35` registers `internal_bp` with `url_prefix="/api/internal"`, so every real request path is `/api/internal/...` and never matches; the guard returns None for all of them. `internal_bp` is also the one blueprint that never calls `before_request(require_session)` (only `api_bp` does, api.py:16), so no session is required either.
findings.impact: Anonymous callers reach DELETE /api/internal/tenants/<id> (deletes every posting for a tenant), POST /api/internal/reindex, POST /api/internal/import and GET /api/internal/status. Destructive, unauthenticated tenant data loss.
findings.recommendation: Compare against the mounted prefix (`/api/internal`) or, better, attach the guard as `internal_bp.before_request` together with `require_session` so the check cannot drift from the mount point again.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 01 (ignore_hypothetical_misuse): this is not a hypothetical caller misusing an API; the mismatch is between two literals inside this repository (auth.py:13 and app.py:35).

mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; both the constant and the `url_prefix=` argument was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.
mantis-review constraint 13 (verify_attacker_control_of_source): the trusted-origin dismissal does not fire; ingress point is any unauthenticated HTTP request to /api/internal/* (app.py:35).

findings.title: Unauthenticated cross-tenant ledger export through the current_tenant() query-string fallback
findings.evidence: `current_tenant()` returns `request.args.get("tenant")` whenever `g.user` is None (auth.py:92-95). `reports_bp` never registers `require_session` (grep for require_session finds only api.py:16), and all three of its views call `current_tenant()` (reports.py:50, 72, 91). `GET /reports/export.csv?tenant=<victim>` therefore returns up to 100000 postings for an arbitrary tenant with no credentials.
findings.impact: Anonymous full-ledger disclosure for every tenant: entry ids, account codes, amounts and memos via /reports/export.csv, /reports/statement and /reports/trial-balance.
findings.recommendation: Register `reports_bp.before_request(require_session)` and derive the tenant only from `g.user`; give the nightly export job its own service credential instead of an unauthenticated query parameter.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 02 (ignore_missing_hygiene): this is not missing defence-in-depth: the fallback is the only tenant selector on an unauthenticated blueprint, so it is the primary authorization decision.

mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the fallback branch and the three call sites was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.
mantis-review constraint 13 (verify_attacker_control_of_source): the trusted-origin dismissal does not fire; ingress point is `?tenant=` on GET /reports/* (reports.py:50).

findings.title: Remote code execution via pickle.loads on a client-supplied draft blob
findings.evidence: `blob = (request.form.get("state") or "").encode("ascii")` then `state = pickle.loads(base64.b64decode(blob))` (api.py:78-79). The value is taken straight from the request form with no signature, no allowlist and no safe unpickler.
findings.impact: Any authenticated tenant user executes arbitrary Python in the ledger process (pickle `__reduce__`), reaching the database credentials, the import volume and the session secret.
findings.recommendation: Serialise drafts as JSON, or sign the blob with `itsdangerous` and verify before unpickling; never call `pickle.loads` on request data.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 08 (intrinsic_security_flaws): rule 08's save condition applies: a deserialization sink fed directly from request data is an intrinsic flaw in this function's own logic.

mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the pickle import and the loads() call was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.
mantis-review constraint 13 (verify_attacker_control_of_source): the trusted-origin dismissal does not fire; ingress point is `request.form["state"]` at api.py:78.

findings.title: Bulk importer bypasses Posting.clean(), and the statement view then renders memos as trusted markup
findings.evidence: `Posting.clean()` (models.py:60-80) is the documented invariant for every row that lands in `postings`: it enforces the account-code shape and runs `bleach.clean(...)` over the memo. `import_batch` writes with `db.session.bulk_insert_mappings(Posting, mappings)` (importer.py:82), which inserts dicts without instantiating the model, so `clean()` never runs on the imported rows. `reports.py:64` then wraps the stored memo in `Markup(p.memo or "")`, explicitly marking it safe, and the Jinja template interpolates it unescaped (reports.py:30).
findings.impact: A memo cell in an imported CSV carrying `<script>` or an event handler executes in the browser of any accountant opening /reports/statement; the account-code invariant is also unenforced on this path.
findings.recommendation: Route the importer through `Posting(**row).clean()` (or apply `bleach.clean` to the mapping before the bulk insert) and sanitise at render time instead of trusting the column with `Markup`.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 05 (no_security_flaw_stretching): this is not stretching a mitigation: the bleach mitigation exists on the ORM path and is simply not on the bulk path, which is a second write path to the same column.

mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; bulk_insert_mappings, clean() and the Markup() wrapper was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.

mantis-review constraint 13 (verify_attacker_control_of_source): the trusted-origin dismissal does not fire; ingress point is memo column of a staged CSV, reached via POST /api/internal/import (internal.py:33).

findings.title: Hardcoded fallback SECRET_KEY signs the session cookie
findings.evidence: `SECRET_KEY = os.environ.get("LEDGER_SECRET_KEY", "ledger-flow-default-secret")` (config.py:15). The comment on line 14 states it signs the session cookie and the CSRF tokens. Nothing fails closed when `LEDGER_SECRET_KEY` is absent, and `load()` defaults to `ProductionConfig` (config.py:50).
findings.impact: If the variable is unset in any environment, anyone can mint a Flask session cookie with an arbitrary `uid`, which `load_session` turns into `g.user` (auth.py:24-34): full account impersonation, including the `accountant` role gate.
findings.recommendation: Raise at start-up when `LEDGER_SECRET_KEY` is missing in a non-testing config, as the code already does for the internal token (`if not expected: abort(403)`).

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 08 (intrinsic_security_flaws): rule 08's save condition applies: a static secret embedded in the source is an intrinsic flaw independent of callers.
mantis-review constraint 02 (ignore_missing_hygiene): not a hardcoded mock database: this value is the live signing key whenever the env var is absent.
mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the config constant and its default was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.

findings.title: Maintenance status endpoint discloses the database URI and import root
findings.evidence: `status()` returns `current_app.config["SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI"]` and `IMPORT_ROOT` (internal.py:18-19). The default URI is a DSN (`postgresql+psycopg://ledger@localhost/ledger`, config.py:18) and a deployed one normally carries a password. The endpoint sits under `/api/internal`, which the guard never covers (see the prefix-mismatch finding).
findings.impact: Anonymous callers learn the database DSN (and any credential in it) plus the filesystem root used by the importer, which is the input to the import path.
findings.recommendation: Remove the connection string from the response and gate the blueprint behind the internal-token check plus a session.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 02 (ignore_missing_hygiene): not a missing-header hygiene item: the handler actively serialises a credential-bearing configuration value into an HTTP response.

mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the two config keys in the jsonify call was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.
mantis-review constraint 13 (verify_attacker_control_of_source): the trusted-origin dismissal does not fire; ingress point is GET /api/internal/status from any unauthenticated client.

findings.title: Authentication bypass: RequireSession falls back to ParseLegacy, which never verifies the signature
findings.evidence: `Verifier.Parse` is strict (HS256 only, `jwt.WithExpirationRequired`, secret checked) but when it returns an error `RequireSession` retries with `token.ParseLegacy(raw)` (auth.go:51-61). `ParseLegacy` (token.go:67-87) splits on '.', base64-decodes **only** `parts[1]` and json-unmarshals it into `Claims`. No key, no MAC, no algorithm check. The resulting `claims.Subject`, `claims.TenantID` and `claims.Role` are written into the request `Scope` (auth.go:63-68).
findings.impact: Anyone can forge `Authorization: Bearer aa.<base64({"sub":"victim","role":"admin","tid":"other-tenant"})>.bb` and become any user in any tenant with any role. Every handler behind the session group, and `middleware.RequireRole`, trust this Scope.
findings.recommendation: Delete the legacy fallback, or verify legacy envelopes against the same secret before accepting them; never accept a claim set that has not been MAC-verified.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 09 (verify_mitigations_pragmatically): the strict `Parse` mitigation exists but is not the only path: the error branch reaches an unverified parser, so the mitigation is bypassable rather than effective.

mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the fallback call at auth.go:56 and the body of ParseLegacy was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.
mantis-review constraint 13 (verify_attacker_control_of_source): the trusted-origin dismissal does not fire; ingress point is `Authorization` header at auth.go:45 (bearer()).

findings.title: The /v1/sync route group carries no session middleware and resolves the device from the query string
findings.evidence: `r.Route("/v1/sync", ...)` attaches only `chimw.Timeout` and `middleware.MaxBytes` (router.go:53-60) — unlike the group above it, which uses `middleware.RequireSession` (router.go:41). `SyncHandler.resolveDevice` returns `middleware.ScopeFrom(ctx).DeviceID` if set and otherwise `r.URL.Query().Get("device_id")` (sync.go:39-44); with no session middleware the Scope is always the zero value, so the query parameter always wins.
findings.impact: `GET /v1/sync/delta?device_id=<victim>` streams up to 5000 records of any device with no credentials, and `POST /v1/sync/push?device_id=<victim>` writes records attributed to that device's owner (`OwnerOfDevice`, sync.go:95).
findings.recommendation: Add `sr.Use(middleware.RequireSession(deps.Tokens))` to the sync group and remove the query-string device fallback, or bind it to a paired device proven by the session.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 01 (ignore_hypothetical_misuse): not a hypothetical caller: the route table in this file is what omits the middleware.
mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the router group and resolveDevice was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.
mantis-review constraint 13 (verify_attacker_control_of_source): the trusted-origin dismissal does not fire; ingress point is `?device_id=` at sync.go:43.

findings.title: Path traversal in the attachment handler on an unauthenticated route
findings.evidence: `os.Open(filepath.Join(h.attachDir, name))` where `name := r.URL.Query().Get("name")` (sync.go:128-134). The only check is that the name is non-empty; `filepath.Join` cleans the path but does not confine it, so `..` segments escape `attachDir`. The route is registered in the `/v1/sync` group, which has no session middleware.
findings.impact: Anonymous arbitrary file read from the service container (`/v1/sync/attachment?name=../../../../etc/passwd`, or the process environment / mounted secrets), returned as `application/octet-stream`.
findings.recommendation: Reject names containing a separator or `..` (or match an opaque-id regex), then verify `filepath.Clean` of the joined path still has `attachDir` as a prefix; use `os.Root`/`openat` semantics where available.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 09 (verify_mitigations_pragmatically): there is no mitigation to credit: `filepath.Join` normalises but does not constrain, and no prefix check follows.
mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the Join call and the query read was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.
mantis-review constraint 13 (verify_attacker_control_of_source): the trusted-origin dismissal does not fire; ingress point is `?name=` at sync.go:128.

findings.title: SQL injection through the sort column of the activity feed
findings.evidence: `q := fmt.Sprintf("... ORDER BY %s DESC LIMIT 500", sortColumn)` (queries.go:163-168). `sortColumn` comes from `r.URL.Query().Get("sort")` in `SyncHandler.ListRecords` (sync.go:113-117) with no allowlist — only an empty-string default. The `ownerID` bind parameter is unaffected by the injected fragment.
findings.impact: An authenticated caller injects into the ORDER BY clause of a live query (subselect-based boolean/error oracles in PostgreSQL), reading data outside the owner scope the `WHERE owner_id = $1` clause was meant to enforce.
findings.recommendation: Map the segmented-control value through a fixed allowlist (`updated_at`, `kind`, `id`) and fall back to the default for anything else; never interpolate an identifier taken from the request.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 04 (avoid_pedantic_linting): not pedantic linting of a safe library: the surrounding query is parameterised precisely because the driver supports it, and this one identifier is concatenated instead.

mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the Sprintf and the handler's query read was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.
mantis-review constraint 13 (verify_attacker_control_of_source): the trusted-origin dismissal does not fire; ingress point is `?sort=` at sync.go:113.

findings.title: Device import trusts the client-supplied owner_id and writes records for other accounts
findings.evidence: `DeviceHandler.Import` decodes `records[]` and passes them straight to `h.repo.BulkInsertRecords(r.Context(), body.Records)` (device.go:81-95); `scope.UserID` is read at line 60 of the neighbouring handlers but never used here. `BulkInsertRecords` inserts `rec.OwnerID` verbatim and its upsert is `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET body = EXCLUDED.body` with **no** owner predicate (queries.go:129-131) — contrast `UpsertRecord`, which does carry `WHERE records.owner_id = $2` (queries.go:115).
findings.impact: Any authenticated user inserts or overwrites the body of any record id belonging to any other user or tenant: cross-tenant data tampering and, by choosing existing ids, silent corruption of other tenants' data.
findings.recommendation: Ignore `OwnerID` on the wire and stamp `scope.UserID` server-side, and add the `WHERE records.owner_id = $2` guard to the bulk statement so the two write paths agree.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 01 (ignore_hypothetical_misuse): not a hypothetical caller passing a bad parameter: the handler in this repository is the caller, and it forwards the wire value unchanged.

mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the handler, the struct tag `json:"owner_id"` and the conflict clause was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.
mantis-review constraint 13 (verify_attacker_control_of_source): the trusted-origin dismissal does not fire; ingress point is `records[].owner_id` in the POST /v1/devices/import body (device.go:83).

findings.title: The nginx office-only allowlist guards /internal/, but the operator console is mounted at /ops
findings.evidence: `location /internal/ { allow 10.20.0.0/16; allow 10.30.4.0/24; deny all; proxy_pass http://relay_app; }` (relay.conf:25-31). The application mounts the operator routes at `/ops`: `Mount("/ops", routes=admin_routes)` (main.py:28). No location block matches `/ops/`, so those requests take `location / { proxy_pass http://relay_app; }` (relay.conf:56) with no `allow`/`deny`. routes_admin.py:3-5 states in its module docstring that the handlers do not re-check staff membership because the edge is assumed to filter them.
findings.impact: The entire operator surface (`/ops/status`, `/ops/flags`, `/ops/replay`, `DELETE /ops/tenants/{id}`) is reachable from the public internet, and the handlers deliberately perform no membership check of their own.
findings.recommendation: Change the block to `location /ops/`, and stop relying on a network ACL as the only authorization for staff endpoints — enforce a role check inside the handlers.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 02 (ignore_missing_hygiene): not defence-in-depth: this ACL is the sole documented authorization control for the operator surface, per routes_admin.py's own docstring.

mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the location block and the Mount prefix was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.
mantis-review constraint 13 (verify_attacker_control_of_source): the trusted-origin dismissal does not fire; ingress point is any internet client requesting /ops/* (main.py:28).

findings.title: /ops/status is on the public-path allowlist and returns the database URL
findings.evidence: `PUBLIC_PATHS` contains `"/ops/status"` (deps.py:13) and `SessionAuthMiddleware.dispatch` returns early for any path `is_public_path()` accepts (middleware.py:43-45). The handler serialises `settings.database_url` (routes_admin.py:26), which `docker-compose.yml:21` sets to `postgresql://relay:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db:5432/relay`. Combined with the `/ops` vs `/internal/` prefix mismatch above, no network ACL covers it either.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated disclosure of the Postgres username, password and host, plus the template directory and process id — a direct path to the database if it is reachable.
findings.recommendation: Drop `database_url` (and `template_dir`) from the payload, and remove `/ops/status` from `PUBLIC_PATHS`; expose an unauthenticated liveness probe that returns only a status string.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 02 (ignore_missing_hygiene): not an information-leak nit: the leaked value is a live credential-bearing DSN, not a version banner.

mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the allowlist entry and the JSONResponse body was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.

findings.title: Operator handlers accept any authenticated session; there is no role check

findings.recommendation: Use `crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret)` over a canonical, length-delimited encoding of the fields (e.g. `${key.length}:${key}|${expiresAt}`).

findings.title: Prototype pollution in the recursive defaults merge
findings.evidence: `for (const key of Object.keys(source))` with `applyDefaults(target[key], value)` and `target[key] = value` (schema.js:92-102) and no rejection of `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype`. `JSON.parse` creates `__proto__` as an own enumerable property, so `Object.keys` yields it and `target['__proto__']` resolves to `Object.prototype`. A repo-wide grep finds no caller: the function is only exported (schema.js:107).
findings.impact: If a route ever merges a request body with this helper — its docstring says it merges 'the tenant's saved preferences under the values supplied for this run' — an attacker pollutes `Object.prototype`. No reachable path exists in the tree as committed.
findings.recommendation: Skip the three dangerous keys, use `Object.create(null)` for accumulators, or replace the helper with `structuredClone` plus explicit field copies.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 06 (evaluate_questionable_file_paths): the path was traced rather than dismissed on its location; the helper simply has no caller yet, hence probable and low.
mantis-review constraint 08 (intrinsic_security_flaws): rule 08's save condition applies: the unguarded key walk is a flaw in the function's own logic, reportable without a live caller.

findings.title: Headless Chromium renders job-controlled HTML with --no-sandbox
findings.evidence: `execFileAsync('chromium-headless', ['--no-sandbox', '--print-to-pdf=' + out, ...])` (render.js:32-41). The HTML it loads embeds a stylesheet URL and a manifest value fetched from `baseUrl` (render.js:51, 57), which the retry path lets a tenant control. Arguments are passed as an array, so there is no shell injection, and `width` is coerced with `Number()`.
findings.impact: A browser-engine exploit reached through attacker-influenced content runs with no sandbox, i.e. directly as the worker user, which also holds the export filesystem and S3 write privileges.
findings.recommendation: Drop `--no-sandbox` and give the container the `SYS_ADMIN`/seccomp profile Chromium's sandbox needs, or run the renderer in a separate least-privileged container.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 02 (ignore_missing_hygiene): not a missing header: an isolation feature is explicitly disabled on a process that parses attacker-influenced input.

mantis-review constraint 03 (require_strict_reproducibility): strict reproducibility does not hold on its own: exploiting it needs a separate browser vulnerability, so this is reported as low/probable hardening rather than a triggerable flaw.

findings.title: The production API task role is granted the AdministratorAccess managed policy
findings.evidence: `tierPolicies = { standard: 'ReadOnlyAccess', ops: 'AdministratorAccess' }` (environments.ts:26-30) and `prod.apiTier = 'ops'` (environments.ts:68). `ServiceRole`'s constructor calls `attachTierPolicy(this.role, props.cfg)` (service-role.ts:35), which resolves `cfg.tierPolicies[cfg.apiTier]` and attaches it (service-role.ts:44-45). That role is the `taskRole` of the internet-facing Fargate API (api-stack.ts:33-47, 76-93).
findings.impact: Any code execution, SSRF-to-metadata or container escape in the production API container yields full administrative control of AWS account 000000000003 — the maximum possible blast radius from a single application bug.
findings.recommendation: Never attach `AdministratorAccess` to a task role. Give the API only the grants it already receives explicitly (`grantArtifacts`, `grantQueue`, `secret.grantRead`) and move break-glass/migration duties to a separate role assumed by a human or a pipeline with MFA/approval.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 02 (ignore_missing_hygiene): not defence-in-depth: this is the privilege the running production workload actually holds.

mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the tier map, prod.apiTier and attachTierPolicy was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.

mantis-review constraint 13 (verify_attacker_control_of_source): the trusted-origin dismissal does not apply: the excessive grant is what converts any of the other application-layer ingress points into account compromise.

findings.title: The shared artifact bucket is anonymously readable in production and holds tenant documents and exports
findings.evidence: When `publicRead` is set the construct relaxes `blockPublicAccess` to `{ blockPublicPolicy: false, restrictPublicBuckets: false }` (bucket.ts:33-39) and adds a policy statement granting `s3:GetObject` to `iam.AnyPrincipal()` on `this.bucket.arnForObjects('*')` — the whole bucket, not an assets prefix (bucket.ts:56-63). `data-stack.ts:28-32` instantiates it with `publicRead: cfg.assetsPublic`, and `prod.assetsPublic = true` (environments.ts:64). The comment at data-stack.ts:26-27 states this one bucket holds 'the brand assets the CDN pulls, the rendered documents and the tenant data exports'.
findings.impact: Every rendered customer document and every tenant data export in production is readable by any anonymous caller who can name or enumerate the key.
findings.recommendation: Scope the anonymous statement to the assets prefix (`arnForObjects('assets/*')`), or better, split the buckets and serve the CDN origin through an OAC-restricted CloudFront distribution while keeping documents and exports fully private.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 02 (ignore_missing_hygiene): not hygiene: an explicit AnyPrincipal Allow on every object is the operative access-control decision.

mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the policy statement, the blockPublicAccess override and prod.assetsPublic was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.
mantis-review constraint 13 (verify_attacker_control_of_source): the trusted-origin dismissal does not fire; ingress point is anonymous s3:GetObject against any object key in the bucket.

findings.title: Production database instance is created with publiclyAccessible: true
findings.evidence: `publiclyAccessible: true` on the `rds.DatabaseInstance` (data-stack.ts:60), justified by a comment about an analytics warehouse in another account pulling nightly over the public endpoint. The instance is otherwise placed in `PRIVATE_ISOLATED` subnets (data-stack.ts:48), and the only remaining control is `databaseSg`, which admits `serviceSg` and `bastionSg` (network-stack.ts:76-85).
findings.impact: The instance is given a publicly resolvable endpoint, so the security group becomes the single control between the internet and the production database; a single over-broad SG rule (the dev environment already ships `0.0.0.0/0` for the bastion) exposes Postgres directly.
findings.recommendation: Keep the instance private and give the warehouse a cross-account path that does not require a public endpoint — VPC peering, PrivateLink, or an export to S3 that the other account reads.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 02 (ignore_missing_hygiene): not defence-in-depth: this flag decides whether the database has an internet-routable endpoint at all.

mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the property and the subnet/SG context was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.
mantis-review constraint 09 (verify_mitigations_pragmatically): the security-group mitigation is real but partial, so the finding is rated medium rather than dismissed.

findings.title: The API role is granted object access to the entire shared bucket because the prefix argument is omitted
findings.evidence: `grantArtifacts(serviceRole.role, props.artifacts.bucket)` is called with two arguments (api-stack.ts:39); the third parameter defaults to `prefix = ''` (service-role.ts:52-56), so the policy resources become `bucket.arnForObjects('*')` and the ListBucket condition becomes `s3:prefix: ['*']` (service-role.ts:60, 67). The function's own docstring says 'Pass the prefix the service writes under so the grant stays scoped to it.'
findings.impact: The API task can read, overwrite and delete every object in the shared bucket, which per data-stack.ts:26-27 includes every other tenant's rendered documents and data exports.
findings.recommendation: Pass the per-service prefix the docstring calls for, and make the parameter required so the scoping cannot be skipped silently.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 01 (ignore_hypothetical_misuse): not hypothetical misuse of an API: the omission is at the only call site of the function, in this repository.

mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the two-argument call and the default parameter was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.

findings.title: Container environment pairs a wildcard CORS origin with credentialed CORS
findings.evidence: `environment: { ..., CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN: '*', CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS: 'true' }` (api-stack.ts:53-61), with a comment explaining that the origin cannot be pinned because tenants use their own subdomains and an embedded widget.
findings.impact: Browsers reject literal `*` with credentials, so an application handed this pair almost always implements it by reflecting the request Origin — exactly the pattern that makes every credentialed cross-origin read succeed (the sibling edge-relay service in this corpus does precisely that).
findings.recommendation: Ship a regex or list of permitted tenant subdomains and have the application echo only matching origins; keep credentials off the widget endpoints entirely.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 01 (ignore_hypothetical_misuse): the consuming image is not in this tree, but the configuration pair itself is the defect and is fully specified here.
mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the two environment entries was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.
mantis-review constraint 03 (require_strict_reproducibility): the flaw is a static configuration value, not a fragile timing-dependent condition.

findings.title: pickEnv silently falls back to the dev configuration when BEACON_ENV is unset or misspelled
findings.evidence: `return environments[name ?? ''] ?? dev;` (environments.ts:83). `bin/beacon.ts:14` calls it with `process.env.BEACON_ENV ?? app.node.tryGetContext('env')`, so an unset variable, a typo (`prd`, `production`) or a missing pipeline export resolves to `dev` — which carries `adminCidrs: ['0.0.0.0/0']`, `assetsPublic: true` and `ephemeral: true` (RemovalPolicy.DESTROY plus `autoDeleteObjects`, bucket.ts:41-44).
findings.impact: A deployment intended for staging or prod silently synthesises the dev posture: SSH open to the internet, a public bucket, and stacks whose data is destroyed on teardown.
findings.recommendation: Throw on an unrecognised or absent name (`const cfg = environments[name]; if (!cfg) throw new Error(...)`) so the pipeline fails loudly instead of degrading.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 01 (ignore_hypothetical_misuse): not hypothetical caller misuse: the fallback is written into the resolver itself and the caller passes a possibly-undefined value by design.

mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the nullish-coalescing fallback and the bin/ call site was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.

findings.title: The dev bastion security group accepts SSH from the entire internet
findings.evidence: `dev.adminCidrs = ['0.0.0.0/0']` (environments.ts:36) is iterated in `NetworkStack` to add `bastionSg.addIngressRule(ec2.Peer.ipv4(cidr), ec2.Port.tcp(22), ...)` (network-stack.ts:52-58). `bastionSg` is in turn allowed into `databaseSg` on 5432 (network-stack.ts:81-85).
findings.impact: The dev jump host is exposed to internet-wide SSH brute-force and 0-day scanning, and it is one hop from the dev database. `pickEnv`'s dev fallback means any environment that loses `BEACON_ENV` inherits this rule.
findings.recommendation: Use the same declared operator ranges as staging/prod, or replace the bastion with SSM Session Manager and remove port 22 ingress entirely.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 06 (evaluate_questionable_file_paths): the path was traced rather than dismissed for being a dev configuration: `pickEnv` makes dev the fallback for every unlabelled deployment.

mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; the CIDR list and the addIngressRule loop was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.

findings.title: Chain: unauthenticated import to unauthenticated stored XSS on any tenant's statement
findings.evidence: Step 1 — `POST /api/internal/import` needs no session and no internal token, because `enforce_internal_token` tests `/internal` while `app.py:35` mounts the blueprint at `/api/internal` and `internal_bp` never registers `require_session`. Step 2 — the handler calls `importer.import_batch` with a caller-chosen `file` and `tenant` (internal.py:33-38), and `import_batch` writes through `bulk_insert_mappings`, which never runs `Posting.clean()`, so the memo skips `bleach.clean` (importer.py:82, models.py:77). Step 3 — `GET /reports/statement?tenant=<any>` needs no session either, because `reports_bp` has no `require_session` and `current_tenant()` accepts `?tenant=` (auth.py:95), and it renders the memo through `Markup()` (reports.py:64), i.e. unescaped.
findings.impact: A single unauthenticated request stores attacker markup under an arbitrary tenant, and a second unauthenticated URL serves it back as HTML to whoever opens the statement — including the accountants whose sessions the API blueprint protects. The three defects individually look moderate; composed, they are an unauthenticated stored-XSS delivery channel into staff browsers.
findings.recommendation: Fix the prefix comparison, attach `require_session` to `reports_bp` and `internal_bp`, sanitise on the bulk import path, and stop wrapping stored text in `Markup`. Any one of the four breaks the chain; all four are needed to close the individual issues.

triage.reason: mantis-review constraint 05 (no_security_flaw_stretching): not an invented adjacent class: each of the three links is an independently verified finding in this same report, and the composition uses no additional assumption.

mantis-review constraint 12 (ensure_source_code_coherence): the anti-hallucination dismissal does not fire; all three links at their cited files and lines was read at the cited path and line in the target tree.

mantis-review constraint 13 (verify_attacker_control_of_source): the trusted-origin dismissal does not fire; ingress point is an unauthenticated POST /api/internal/import, then an unauthenticated GET /reports/statement?tenant=.
